entities.summary: Rhetorical device that manipulates language to convey meaning contrary to literal interpretation. Irony's roots in ancient Greece, where it was used to subvert expectations and challenge social norms. This literary technique has been employed by philosophers, poets, and politicians to make pointed critiques of power and authority. From Sophocles' tragic heroes to Shakespeare's complex characters, irony has played a crucial role in shaping the development of Western literature. By exposing the contradictions and hypocrisies of human endeavor, irony has served as a powerful tool for social commentary and critique. This device's versatility has led to its use in various forms of communication, from satire to advertising, where it is often employed to create a sense of irony or incongruity. In the context of historical events, irony has played a significant role in shaping public opinion and challenging dominant narratives. By analyzing the ways in which irony has been used throughout history, we can gain a deeper understanding of the complex relationships between language, power, and human behavior. Through its enduring influence on literature and communication, irony continues to shape our understanding of the world and our place within it.
